item.title: IOC to buy crude, LPG ships as West Asia crisis exposes shipping risks
item.description: State-owned Indian Oil Corporation plans to acquire crude oil and liquefied petroleum gas carriers of its own as disruptions to shipping around the Strait of Hormuz and soaring freight costs prompt India's largest oil refiner to strengthen control over its energy supply chain. The company's board has already approved the purchase of a few vessels, and tenders were issued several months ago, Director of Finance Anuj Jain said during its second-quarter earnings call. "The country needs oil sector companies to focus more on the shipping area now," Jain said, adding that IOC was also exploring the possibility of building ships in India under the government's Make in India initiative. The move marks a potential shift in the company's shipping strategy, which has traditionally relied on a mix of time-charter and voyage-chartered vessels. item.title: SBI expands US footprint as California subsidiary opens first Texas branch
item.description: State Bank of India (California), a wholly-owned subsidiary of India's largest lender State Bank of India (SBI), has inaugurated its new branch in Frisco, Texas. This opening marks the subsidiary's first physical expansion beyond California, with its US branches now at eight locations. The inauguration ceremony was led by SBI Group Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty, alongside Consul General of India in Houston, DC Manjunath and Frisco Mayor Mark Hill. Located in the rapidly growing North Dallas region, the new Frisco branch is designed to offer a full suite of retail and business banking services. These include personal and business deposits, commercial lending, and international remittances, tailored specifically for individuals, professionals, entrepreneurs, and corporate entities across North Texas. In addition, Y Combinator, through its arm YC Holdings II, LLC, disposed of 5.50 crore shares on the BSE. item.title: Noel Tata to step down as Voltas chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus
item.description: Noel N Tata, Chairman of Tata Trusts, has been appointed as Chairman Emeritus of Voltas, a day after he retired as Chairman and Director of the leading cooling products maker. Noel Tata will retire as Chairman and Director of Voltas Ltd on November 11, 2026, upon attaining the age of superannuation under Tata Group governance guidelines. Following his retirement, "the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing. The Companies Act 2013 mandates that any managing director or whole-time director cannot be appointed or continue employment if they are 70 years of age or older. Noel Tata, who was born on November 12, 1956, will turn 70 on November 12, 2026. He has been associated with Voltas since 2003. item.bs:keywords: Noel Tata, Voltas, Voltas chairman, chairman emeritus, Sunil D'Souza, Tata Group, Tata Trusts, Voltas board, leadership change, Companies Act 2013, superannuation

item.title: Bharti Airtel reclaims 2nd spot in mcap rankings, overtakes Jio Platforms
item.description: Bharti Airtel on Friday reclaimed the title of the country's second most valuable company by market valuation, overtaking Jio Platforms. At market close, Bharti Airtel shares ended 1.66 per cent higher at Rs 2,096.25 on the BSE. During the day, the stock climbed 2.81 per cent to Rs 2,120. However, the stock of Jio Platforms dipped 0.90 per cent to end at Rs 1,405.75. Intraday, it declined 2 per cent to Rs 1,390. The market valuation of Bharti Airtel stood at Rs 13 lakh crore, while that of Jio Platforms was Rs 12.94 lakh crore. Jio Platforms Ltd, the Reliance Industries-backed digital services company, on October 28 became the second most valuable Indian company by market valuation following an impressive debut on the Dalal Street. Reliance Industries continues to remain the most valued domestic firm, with a market valuation of Rs 17,83,723.93 crore.
